newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon says no big change in prospects.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon says no big change in prospects.

text.p: Raytheon Co said Tuesday that while it is not satisfied with its operating performance in the third quarter, there has been no dramatic change in the company's prospects.
The company issued a statement accompanying its earnings report saying its strategy is sound, its fundamentals are strong, and it is taking aggressive steps to resume earnings growth.

Raytheon said its lower than anticipated operating income for the third quarter was primarily attributable to lower revenue and increased sales promotion costs in the company's appliance sector and delays in contract awards at Raytheon Engineers & Constructors.

The company said operating income was down 15.0 percent from last year's level after adjusting for the 1995 sale of D.C. Heath and the effects of strike-related losses resulting from the now-settled eight-week strike at Cedarapids, the manufacturing arm of Raytheon Engineers & Constructors.
The company said this shortfall in operating income was offset by $75.0 million in R&D tax credits and associated interest income.
